summary: Imported models now behave like in-app-trained ones: their class labels are auto-detected and synonym-mapped instead of typed. (1) On import, the backend loads the .pt via ultralytics and reads model.names (lowercased, in class-index order); these authoritative labels override any typed Classes since they are exactly what the worker emits. The Import form's Classes field is now optional (auto-detected; kept only as a fallback when Python/ultralytics is unavailable), and the success message reports the detected classes. (2) On activation, UpsertTrained now folds known label synonyms into the matching built-in canonical class instead of registering a disconnected standalone class — e.g. a fire model emitting 'flame'/'wildfire' is added to the Fire hazard's members (and 'smoking'/'white smoke' to Smoke), so a rule targeting Fire/Smoke fires on those labels with no manual mapping. A new labelSynonyms table (fire/smoke families seeded) drives this and is the place to add spellings for future hazard models. Labels with no synonym match still register as their own trained class as before.
compatibility: Backward compatible. If label auto-detection fails (no Python/ultralytics configured), the importer falls back to the user-supplied Classes. Synonym folding only adds members to a canonical class that already exists and never removes or renames anything; unknown labels behave exactly as before. Auto-detection adds a one-time ultralytics load (a few seconds) to the import request.
